T: Donut holes, birthday cake and one very nice sweater.
D: A detective investigates the death of a crime novelist after his 85th birthday party, with the whole family as suspects.
P: Serve the donut holes when Blanc starts on his donut theory.
S: Benoit Blanc's theory of the donut hole
Small balls of yeasted dough fried at 175C until puffed and golden, rolled in cinnamon sugar while hot.
Harlan's 85th birthday party at the mansion

Little French cheese puffs of choux pastry and gruyère, baked hollow, light and golden with a salty crust of extra cheese. Heat the oven to 200C. Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g plain flour until it pulls away from the sides, then cool 5 minutes. Beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy, then 120g grated gruyère, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg. Pipe 24 small mounds onto lined trays, top with 30g more gruyère and bake 22 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm.

Clams, smoky bacon, potato and onion simmered in a thick creamy broth with thyme, served in small cups with oyster crackers and chives. Fry 120g diced bacon until crisp. Add 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml fish stock, 400ml milk, 400g diced potato and thyme. Simmer 15 minutes. Add 1kg vongole clams, cover and cook 5 minutes until open, then remove the shells. Stir in 150ml cream and season with pepper. Ladle into small cups and top with chives and oyster crackers.
M: the family dinner at the mansion
Beef rib roast seasoned with garlic and thyme, roasted pink and carved at the table with horseradish cream and roast potatoes.
a New England summer classic, Thrombey territory

Chunks of cooked lobster in a lemon, chive and celery mayo, piled into buttered, griddled brioche hot dog rolls with crisp lettuce and a pinch of paprika. Cut the meat from 2 cooked lobsters, about 500g, into chunks. Mix with 80g mayo, 1 finely diced celery stick, 1 tbsp chopped chives, the zest and juice of half a lemon, salt and pepper. Chill 15 minutes. Butter the sides of 4 brioche hot dog rolls and toast in a pan until golden. Line with shredded cos, pile in the lobster and finish with a pinch of paprika and more chives.
W: Rich chocolate layer cake covered in dark chocolate fudge frosting, with candles lit for an 85th birthday.
K: Maple bourbon coffee with whipped cream
the 'my house, my rules, my coffee' mug

Strong hot coffee stirred with maple syrup and a shot of bourbon, poured into big mugs and topped with cold whipped cream and a grating of nutmeg. Brew 800ml strong coffee. Whip 150ml cream with 1 tsp maple syrup to soft peaks. Into each of 4 big mugs pour 1 tbsp maple syrup and 30ml bourbon, then 200ml hot coffee and stir. Spoon the cream on top so it floats and grate over a little nutmeg. Leave out the bourbon for non-drinkers. Make sure everyone gets the right mug.

s.how: Mix 300g flour, 7g dried yeast, 30g sugar, 160ml warm milk, 1 egg and 30g soft butter into a soft dough and prove 1 hour. Roll into 24 small balls, prove 20 minutes, then fry at 175C for 2 minutes until golden. Roll in 100g sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon while hot.

m.note: the family dinner at the mansion
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg beef rib roast with 3 crushed garlic cloves, thyme and salt. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 45 minutes for medium rare, and rest 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes in chunks alongside. Carve at the table with 4 tbsp horseradish cream.

w.how: Beat 200g butter with 250g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 60g cocoa and 250ml milk. Bake in two 20cm tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 100g butter, beat in 150g icing sugar, then stack and frost the layers and add candles.
